sections.skill: Create linear and quadratic equations in two variables and graph them with labels and scales

questions.skill: Create linear and quadratic equations in two variables and graph them with labels and scales
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Tank A has 20 gallons and gains 5 gallons per minute. Tank B starts empty and gains 7 gallons per minute. Write an equation for each tank (y gallons after x minutes). Graph both for 0 ≤ x ≤ 15, label each line, and mark where they meet.
questions.prompt_markup:
Tank A has 20 gallons and gains 5 gallons per minute. Tank B starts empty and gains 7 gallons per minute.
Write an equation for each tank (y gallons after x minutes). Graph both for 0 ≤ x ≤ 15, label each line, and mark where they meet.
questions.correct_answer: Tank A: y = 5x + 20; Tank B: y = 7x
questions.drawing_answer: Line A from (0, 20) to (15, 95) and line B from (0, 0) to (15, 105), each labeled, meeting at (10, 70)
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the two equations, and the two labeled lines meeting at (10, 70).

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 15 and y from 0 to 120. x-axis label "Minutes", y-axis label "Gallons". Nothing is plotted; the student draws on it.

questions.skill: Create linear and quadratic equations in two variables and graph them with labels and scales
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 m. Write an equation for its area A in terms of its width w, and give the values of w that make sense.
questions.prompt_markup:
A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 m.
Write an equation for its area A in terms of its width w, and give the values of w that make sense.
questions.grading_note: Equivalent forms such as A = 20w - w² are correct. Both parts are required.

questions.skill: Create linear and quadratic equations in two variables and graph them with labels and scales
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A ball's height is h = -5t² + 20t meters after t seconds, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. Which axes and scales fit a graph of this equation?
questions.prompt_markup:
A ball's height is h = -5t² + 20t meters after t seconds, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4.
Which axes and scales fit a graph of this equation?

choices.text: Horizontal: time from 0 to 4 seconds; vertical: height from -20 to 0 meters
Horizontal: time t from 0 to 4 seconds; vertical: height h from 0 to 20 meters
Horizontal: height from 0 to 4 meters; vertical: time from 0 to 20 seconds
Horizontal: time from 0 to 20 seconds; vertical: height from 0 to 4 meters

questions.correct_answer: Horizontal: time t from 0 to 4 seconds; vertical: height h from 0 to 20 meters
